planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; native to rich Eastern woodlands and moist limestone-influenced glades.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, mimicking the rich, damp woodland floor and limestone glade edges where this fern is naturally found across the eastern United States. Diplazium pycnocarpon forms upright clumps of narrow, simple, once-divided fronds with a graceful, arching form distinct from the more finely dissected fronds of many other woodland ferns, spreading gradually by rhizome to form loose colonies in favorable sites. The deciduous fronds emerge fresh green in spring and die back to the ground each winter, re-emerging reliably the following year once the clump is established. It combines well with other shade-loving woodland natives such as trillium, wild ginger, and Solomon's seal in naturalistic shade gardens, and needs no special care beyond consistent moisture and rich, organic soil.

common_name: Ursula Red Fern (Deep Burgundy Japanese Painted Fern)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; the deepest red coloring develops with bright, indirect light.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, providing bright indirect light for the most intense foliage color. Ursula Red is a Japanese painted fern selection bred for exceptionally deep, saturated burgundy-red coloring throughout the fronds, considerably darker and richer than the silver-and-maroon coloring of the classic Japanese painted fern, making it a dramatic accent in shaded borders and container plantings. The compact, well-behaved clump stays tidy without spreading aggressively, and the deep red color contrasts strikingly against green-leaved shade companions like hosta, heuchera, and other ferns. Divide congested clumps every few years in early spring, and keep soil consistently moist, since painted fern selections are less drought-tolerant than many tougher native ferns.

common_name: Victoriae Lady Fern (Victorian Crested Lattice-Frond Fern)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Victoriae is a striking Victorian-era lady fern cultivar prized by fern collectors for a genuinely unusual frond structure, in which the leaflets cross and overlap in a distinctive lattice or crisscross pattern rather than lying flat in the typical fern arrangement, creating a lacy, almost woven texture unlike any ordinary fern. This heirloom cultivar has been maintained in cultivation since Victorian times specifically for its ornamental oddity, and it makes a genuine conversation piece and focal point in a shaded fern collection or woodland garden bed. Culture is otherwise identical to standard lady fern: consistent moisture, rich organic soil, and full to partial shade, with clumps dying back each winter and re-emerging reliably each spring.
